questions.q: What is the key difference between passing data through an `@api` property and passing content through a `<slot>`?
options: There is no real difference; slots and @api properties serve the same purpose
An @api property passes data (strings, numbers, objects); a slot passes actual markup, which the child places wherever <slot> appears in its own template
Slots can only pass numbers, never strings or markup
@api properties can only be set once, while slots can be changed repeatedly
questions.explain: @api properties carry data values. A slot is fundamentally different -- it lets a parent hand actual markup to a child, and the child decides where that markup renders inside its own template.

It renders into the named 'header' slot by default

questions.explain: Content with no slot attribute goes into the unnamed default slot. Only content explicitly tagged slot="header" goes into the slot named header.

questions.q: When does a `<slot>`'s fallback content (placed directly inside the `<slot>` tags) actually render?
options: Always, in addition to whatever the parent provides
Only when the parent provides no content for that slot
Only when the component is exposed to Lightning App Builder
Never -- fallback content inside a slot tag is ignored by the framework
questions.explain: Fallback content inside a <slot> tag is a default shown only when the parent doesn't fill that slot with its own content; if the parent does provide content, the fallback is not shown.

questions.q: Why can't a child component's CSS file restyle content the parent placed into one of the child's slots?
options: Because CSS selectors like `p { color: red; }` are invalid inside component CSS files
Because slotted content still belongs to the parent's own shadow tree, even though it visually renders inside the child -- a direct consequence of shadow DOM encapsulation
Because slots do not support any CSS styling at all, from either side
Because only @api properties can be styled, never slotted markup
questions.explain: Even though slotted content visually appears inside the child, it remains part of the parent's own shadow tree. The child's scoped CSS cannot reach across that shadow DOM boundary to restyle it.

questions.q: Per this lesson's guidance, when should a component use a slot instead of an @api property?
options: Whenever the component needs a record Id or a simple status string
When the component provides structure or layout and the actual content varies by caller -- for example a generic card, panel, or modal shell
Slots and @api properties are never used in the same component
Only when the component needs to call Apex
questions.explain: @api properties fit specific values a child needs to do its job. Slots fit components that provide structure or layout where the actual content varies by caller -- many components use both at once for different parts of their template.
